## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD ability to implement per-namespace GitOps, use InitContainers, ConfigMaps, PVCs, and NetworkPolicy; validates YAML tooling, apply flow, and status reporting.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace GitOps design patterns
- InitContainer provisioning and tool installation
- YAML validation with kubeval and yamllint
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for configuration
- PVC-based log streaming and persistence
- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy for egress control
- Drift detection and status reporting via ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for a per-namespace GitOps runner
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gitops-runner
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gitops-runner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gitops-runner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: git-clone
        image: alpine/git:latest
        env:
        - name: REPO_URL
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: repo-url
        - name: TARGET_PATH
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: target-path
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          apk add --no-cache git yq
          git clone $(REPO_URL) /workspace/repo
          cd /workspace/repo
          yq eval '.spec.path = "$(TARGET_PATH)"' . > manifests.yaml
      containers:
      - name: validator
        image: kubeval/kubeval:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          kubeval /workspace/manifests.yaml > /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          yamllint -d relaxed /workspace/manifests.yaml >> /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          kubectl apply -f /workspace/manifests.yaml --namespace=$(NAMESPACE)
          kubectl get -f /workspace/manifests.yaml -o jsonpath='{.status}' > /gitops-status
      volumes:
      - name: workspace
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: gitops-logs
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose common CKAD primitives into a cohesive, maintainable per-namespace app: InitContainer logic, ConfigMap-driven behavior, TLS handling, and network isolation.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer installs rendering tool and pre-processes inputs
- ConfigMap and Secret drive runtime config and secrets
- Sidecar for TLS rotation and secret refresh
- Readiness/Liveness probes for quick failure detection
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricts egress to internal endpoints

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: docs-portal
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: docs-portal
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: docs-portal
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: docs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: docs-pvc
        - name: tls-cert
          secret:
            secretName: docs-tls
      initContainers:
        - name: render-md
          image: pandoc/pandoc:latest
          command: ["sh", "-c", "cp -r /docs/* /rendered/; pandoc -f markdown -t html /docs/*.md -o /rendered/index.html"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: docs
              mountPath: /docs
            - name: rendered
              mountPath: /rendered
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:stable
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80
          volumeMounts:
            - name: rendered
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /
              port: 80
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /
              port: 80
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
```

- Kubernetes Job with backoff and deadline

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests your ability to design an isolated audit pattern with in-cluster API access, RBAC scoping, and security boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped RBAC for fine-grained access control
- In-cluster API access using Secrets and ConfigMaps
- PVC-backed persistent logs and InitContainers for tooling
- NetworkPolicy for egress control to restrict traffic to the collector
- Health checks (readiness/liveness probes) for reliability

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-baseline
  namespace: example
data:
  baseline.json: |
    {"pods": [], "services": []}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: audit-auth
  namespace: example
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: " collector-auth-token"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: audit-logs
  namespace: example
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: audit-agent
  namespace: example
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: audit-agent
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl jq && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
      containers:
      - name: auditor
        image: your-audit-image:latest
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; do audit.sh; sleep 60; done"]
        env:
        - name: COLLECTOR_URL
          value: "http://collector.audit-system.svc.cluster.local:8080"
        - name: AUTH_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: audit-auth
              key: token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        - name: tools
          mountPath: /tools
        - name: baseline
          mountPath: /baseline
          readOnly: true
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: audit-logs
      - name: tools
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: baseline
        configMap:
          name: audit-baseline
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit-egress-restrict
  namespace: example
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: audit-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: audit-system
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: collector
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8080
```

## Trade-offs
- **Pros**: Namespace isolation ensures audit agents don't interfere; NetworkPolicy provides security; PVC enables log persistence for compliance
- **Cons**: Each namespace requires separate Deployment (use Operator/Controller to automate); InitContainer adds startup latency; per-namespace RBAC management overhead increases with cluster size

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical knowledge of namespace-scoped governance primitives and their impact on scheduling, pod density, and autoscaler behavior.

## Key Concepts
- **ResourceQuota** enforces hard caps on total namespace resource consumption (CPU, memory, pod count, etc.)
- **LimitRange** sets defaults and constraints for individual pod/container resource requests and limits
- Quota enforcement affects scheduler decisions, pod scheduling failures, and autoscaler calculations
- Use `kubectl describe resourcequota <name> --namespace=<ns>` and `kubectl top pod` to monitor usage

## Code Example

```yaml
# Namespace
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: quota-demo
---
# ResourceQuota
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: ns-quota
  namespace: quota-demo
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4"
    requests.memory: "8Gi"
    limits.cpu: "8"
    limits.memory: "16Gi"
    pods: "20"
---
# LimitRange
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: ns-limits
  namespace: quota-demo
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    default:
      cpu: 500m
      memory: 512Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: 250m
      memory: 256Mi
    max:
      cpu: "2"
      memory: "4Gi"
    min:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
---
# Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: quota-demo-app
  namespace: quota-demo
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: demo
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: demo
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 128Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 512Mi
```

## Trade-offs
- **Flexibility vs. Control**: Quotas prevent resource hoarding but require developers to specify requests/limits, increasing YAML complexity
- **Utilization Risk**: Overly restrictive quotas lead to pod scheduling failures; overly generous quotas waste resources
- **Debugging Overhead**: Quota-induced failures (e.g., "pods quota exceeded") add a layer of complexity to troubleshooting
- **Autoscaler Interaction**: VPA/HPA behavior changes when quotas constrain available headroom

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to compose a production-ready backup workflow using core Kubernetes primitives (CronJob, Secret, ConfigMap, PVC, NetworkPolicy) while understanding scope, lifecycle management, and security boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- **CronJob per-namespace scope**: Each namespace runs its own backup Job, ensuring isolation and scope-bound retention
- **InitContainer**: Installs mysqldump and gzip tools at Pod startup before the backup container runs
- **Secrets and ConfigMaps**: Store database credentials securely and retention policies as configuration
- **PVC-backed storage**: Provides persistent storage for backup files independent of Pod lifecycle
- **Probes**: Readiness and liveness probes ensure backup reliability and Pod health
- **NetworkPolicy**: Restricts egress traffic at the namespace level to prevent data exfiltration

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-backup
  namespace: my-namespace
spec:
  schedule: "0 */6 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: debian:latest
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apt-get update && apt-get install -y mysql-client gzip"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: backup-volume
              mountPath: /backups
          containers:
          - name: backup
            image: alpine:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
            args:
            - |
              mysqldump -h $DB_HOST -u $DB_USER -p$DB_PASSWORD $DB_NAME | gzip > /backups/$DATE.sql.gz
              find /backups -name "*.sql.gz" -mtime +$RETENTION_DAYS -delete
            env:
            - name: DB_HOST
              value: "localhost"
            - name: DB_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-creds
                  key: username
            - name: DB_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-creds
                  key: password
            - name: DB_NAME
              value: "appdb"
            - name: DATE
              value: "$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
            - name: RETENTION_DAYS
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: backup-config
                  key: retentionDays
            volumeMounts:
            - name: backup-volume
              mountPath: /backups
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["ls", "/backups"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["ls", "/backups"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
          volumes:
          - name: backup-volume
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: backup-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Trade-offs
- **PVC vs. emptyDir**: PVC provides persistence across Pod restarts but requires pre-provisioned storage; emptyDir is simpler but loses data on Pod termination
- **InitContainer vs. multi-stage image**: InitContainer adds startup overhead; a custom multi-stage image is leaner but requires image maintenance
- **Per-namespace CronJob**: Simplifies scope and retention per namespace but increases operational overhead compared to a centralized cluster-wide solution
- **NetworkPolicy**: Enhances security but requires careful planning of allowed egress rules to avoid breaking legitimate traffic
